meta.description: The Fire and Emergency Services (F&ES) Flight operates 24/7/365 to provide rapid, comprehensive emergency response, including structural fire suppression, Aircraft Rescue and Firefighting (ARFF), hazardous materials (HAZMAT) response, technical rescue, and emergency medical services (EMS). Personnel maintain constant combat and emergency readiness while performing daily vehicle maintenance, equipment testing, facility fire prevention inspections, and rigorous physical and tactical training. Operating in a highly dynamic, industrial, and high-hazard environment, this work center is dedicated to protecting life, property, and mission-critical assets across the installation.
meta.references: Foundational workplace safety and JSTO development requirements are mandated by DAFI 91-202 - The Department of the Air Force (DAF) Mishap Prevention Program (The US Air Force Mishap Prevention Program), DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards (Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire, and Health Standards), and federal OSHA standards under Title 29 CFR § 1910. Operational guidelines, training, and emergency response parameters are dictated by AFMAN 32-1007 (Fire and Emergency Services Flight Operations), alongside overarching DoD policy defined in DoDI 6055.06 and DoDM 6055.06, which ensure adherence to National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) professional qualifications. Furthermore, due to the high-hazard nature of firefighting and medical response, strict occupational health directives apply; these include DAFI 48-137 for the Respiratory Protection Program (governing SCBA use), AFI 48-127 - Occupational Noise and Hearing Conservation Program for the Occupational Noise and Hearing Conservation Program, and 29 CFR § 1910.1030 to ensure compliance with Bloodborne Pathogens standards.
meta.jhaNotes: A comprehensive Job Hazard Analysis (JHA) must address diverse operational risks. Personnel face environmental hazards like seasonal heat and flooding, alongside facility-specific dangers such as faulty electrical equipment, wet floors, high noise, and poor air quality, which are mitigated through regular inspections and mandatory PPE. Highway operations introduce significant risks from managing large apparatus in high-speed traffic and adverse conditions, requiring strict adherence to vehicle placement and safety protocols. Furthermore, emergency medical responses present a primary hazard of exposure to contagious diseases and bloodborne pathogens. This risk is controlled by the mandatory use of specific PPE—including high-risk surgical gloves and eye protection—and adherence to stringent decontamination procedures.

meta.medicalFacility: The Hunters Medical Clinic (Bldg 1033) serves as the primary medical facility on Creech AFB, providing Flight Medicine, Family Health, and outpatient services during duty hours (Monday–Friday). On-base emergencies requiring immediate medical treatment are handled by calling 911 (or 702-404-0911 from a cell phone) to initiate a response from the clinic’s localized ambulance service. For acute or after-hours emergencies, patients are transported to the 24/7 Emergency Department at Mike O'Callaghan Military Medical Center on Nellis AFB or local civilian trauma facilities. Active-duty personnel requiring standard medical treatment must utilize scheduled appointments or the designated morning flight medicine sick call, and they must contact the Nurse Advice Line for off-base urgent care referrals to avoid unauthorized billing.
meta.evacuationRoute: Personnel will evacuate to designated assembly points, ensuring they evacuate all fire vehicles and apparatus from the bays only if it is safe to do so. For personnel in Building 1150, the muster point is the parking lot located to the west of the main entrance. For personnel in Building 85, the evacuation point is the theater parking lot (Bldg. 39). All individuals must remain at their designated assembly point until formally cleared to leave by Senior Fire Officer.

meta.fireEquipmentNotes: Emergency equipment and fire protection systems are strategically located throughout the fire stations for immediate access. Emergency power cutoff panels are situated in the East Side Mechanical Room for Station 1 and the West Side Mechanical Room for Station 2. Fire alarm pull boxes and fire extinguishers are distributed throughout both buildings, primarily near exits and in various other locations around each station. Additionally, a Bomb Threat Checklist is available near the phone and within the Creech Phone Directory for reference during such an event. Supervisors are responsible for showing all personnel the specific locations of this equipment.

meta.trafficSafetyNotes: Personnel must remain aware of local traffic hazards, particularly on I-95, which is prone to construction, peak flow congestion, and hazardous conditions like potholes and flooding after rainstorms. Drivers are required to follow all state and local laws, including speed limits, seat belt use, and the prohibition of cell phone use without a hands-free device. Vehicle-specific safety procedures mandate the use of spotters when backing, careful placement of apparatus on highways to protect responders from traffic, and heightened awareness of noise and air quality hazards from vehicle operations within the station.

selectedModules.title: Hazardous Energy Control
selectedModules.reference: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards, Chapter 21; 29 CFR 1910.147 - The control of hazardous energy (lockout/tagout)
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Train authorized employees to recognize hazardous energy sources, the type and magnitude of energy present, and the methods and means for isolation and control. Train affected employees on the purpose and use of lockout/tagout procedures, and instruct all other employees on the prohibition against restarting locked or tagged equipment.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Document initial and refresher training when job assignments, machines, processes, or energy control procedures change, or when inspections show employee knowledge gaps.

selectedModules.title: Hazard Communication
selectedModules.reference: DAFI 90-821; 29 CFR 1910.1200 - Hazard Communication
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Train personnel on hazardous chemicals in their work area, labeling systems, safety data sheets, and the measures they can take to protect themselves during normal operations and foreseeable emergencies.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Provide HazCom training upon initial assignment, whenever a new chemical hazard is introduced, and when new tasks expose workers to different hazardous materials. Ensure workers know how to access local SDS information and labeling guidance.

selectedModules.title: Bloodborne Pathogens
selectedModules.reference: 29 CFR 1910.1030 - Bloodborne Pathogens
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Provide bloodborne pathogens training at initial assignment and at least annually thereafter, covering exposure control, modes of transmission, and protective measures.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Enroll applicable workers in the local bloodborne pathogens program and ensure exposure control plan requirements, reporting actions, and PPE procedures are covered before task performance.

selectedModules.title: Hearing Conservation
selectedModules.reference: DAFI 48-127; 29 CFR 1910.95 - Occupational noise exposure
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Train noise-exposed employees annually on the effects of noise, the purpose of hearing protectors, the advantages and disadvantages of various protectors, and the purpose of audiometric testing.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Ensure workers enrolled in hearing conservation understand noise hazard areas, double-hearing protection requirements, and local follow-up actions tied to occupational health evaluations.

selectedModules.title: Confined Space Program
selectedModules.reference: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards, Chapter 23; 29 CFR 1910.146 - Permit-required confined spaces
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Train entrants, attendants, supervisors, and rescue personnel so they understand their duties, hazards, signs and symptoms of exposure, communication procedures, and emergency actions before assignment.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Provide duty-specific training for permit-required confined space roles, including monitor use, atmospheric hazards, entry permits, and rescue responsibilities before personnel participate in entries.

selectedModules.title: Respiratory Protection Program
selectedModules.reference: DAFI 48-137; 29 CFR 1910.134 - Respiratory protection
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Train users before respirator use and at least annually on why the respirator is necessary, how improper fit or maintenance can compromise protection, and how to inspect, don, doff, use, and store the respirator.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Document fit testing and occupational health training on AF Form 2767 and ensure wearers understand emergency-use limits, cartridge change-out, cleaning, and medical qualification requirements.

selectedModules.title: Vehicle Mounted Elevated Work Platforms
selectedModules.reference: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards, Chapter 16
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Provide model-specific training, safe operating procedures, fall protection expectations, and emergency lowering actions before use of elevated work platforms.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Use locally approved lesson plans with hands-on demonstration, written testing, and supervisor certification before operators use mobile elevating work platforms.

selectedModules.title: Fall Arrest Systems
selectedModules.reference: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards, Chapter 13; 29 CFR 1910.66 - Powered platforms for building maintenance; 29 CFR 1926.503 - Training requirements
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Train employees exposed to fall hazards to recognize fall hazards and the procedures to minimize them, including use and inspection of fall arrest systems.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Cover anchorage selection, rescue planning, and equipment inspections before personnel use personal fall arrest systems in assigned tasks.
selectedModules.trainingBasis: OSHA 2254 / Walking-Working Surfaces and Fall Protection

selectedModules.title: Explosives Safety Training
selectedModules.reference: DESR 6055.09_DAFMAN 91-201 - Explosives Safety Standards; DAFI 91-202 - The Department of the Air Force (DAF) Mishap Prevention Program
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Use explosives-specific AF lesson plans and local operating instructions. OSHA 2254 includes transportation and explosives references, but the Air Force explosives program should remain the primary training basis for this module.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Provide initial and task-specific explosives safety training using approved lesson plans, local instructions, and quantity-distance / compatibility controls before personnel work with explosives.

selectedModules.title: CPR Training
selectedModules.reference: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards, Chapter 1
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Provide CPR and AED training before assignment where required, and refresh qualification before expiration.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Ensure designated responders maintain current certification and understand location and use of local AED assets under the unit mishap prevention program.

selectedModules.title: Flight Line Driving
selectedModules.reference: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards, Chapter 24
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Provide local flight line driving rules, markings, vehicle lighting requirements, restricted areas, and aircraft hazard awareness before granting driving privileges.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Use installation or unit-approved training and certification for airfield/fight line operations, to include local speed, spotter, and no-lone-zone requirements.
selectedModules.afTrainingBasis: DAFMAN 91-203 / Aircraft Flight Line – Ground Operations and Activities

selectedModules.title: Fetal Protection Program
selectedModules.reference: DAFMAN 48-146
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Provide job-specific hazard awareness for reproductive health risks where occupational exposures may affect pregnant workers or fetuses.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Use occupational and environmental health guidance to discuss declaration options, exposure review, and local work restriction procedures.

selectedModules.title: Medical Surveillance Examination
selectedModules.reference: DAFI 48-145 - Occupational and Environmental Health Program
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Ensure workers understand when medical surveillance examinations are required, how they are scheduled, and why participation is tied to specific exposures.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Cover local scheduling, reporting, and follow-up processes for required occupational and environmental health evaluations.

selectedModules.title: Laser Safety Training
selectedModules.reference: DAFI 48-139
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Provide laser hazard awareness, eyewear, posting, alignment, and beam-control training before personnel work with lasers or enter laser-controlled areas.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Use local laser safety officer guidance and approved operating instructions to cover exposure limits, alignment procedures, and emergency actions.
selectedModules.afTrainingBasis: DAFI 48-139 / Laser and Optical Radiation Protection

selectedModules.title: Active Shooter Response
selectedModules.reference: Installation emergency management guidance / local procedures
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Brief personnel on how to recognize an active shooter event, how to summon help, and how to apply local run-hide-fight guidance based on the facility layout.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Use local emergency response procedures, shelter locations, and mass notification methods applicable to the duty location.

selectedModules.title: Government Vehicle / Utility Vehicle Use
selectedModules.reference: DAFI 91-207; local procedures
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Train vehicle operators on seat belts, speed limits, local traffic hazards, spotter use while backing, and restrictions on electronic device use while driving.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Brief operators on unit-specific government vehicle training requirements, local route restrictions, low-speed vehicle rules, and documentation of qualification.
selectedModules.trainingBasis: OSHA 2254 / Vehicle and Mobile Equipment Concepts

selectedModules.title: Manual Lifting and Material Handling
selectedModules.reference: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards, Chapter 20
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Train workers on proper lifting techniques, team lifting, load assessment, and use of lifting aids to reduce musculoskeletal injury risk.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Provide verbal and written guidance on manual lifting, lifting devices, and local reporting actions for strain or overexertion symptoms.
selectedModules.trainingBasis: OSHA 2254 / Ergonomics and Material Handling Concepts

selectedModules.title: Fire Protection and Prevention
selectedModules.reference: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards; local fire prevention plan
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Train personnel on fire hazards, reporting procedures, extinguisher locations, evacuation routes, pull stations, and local emergency response actions.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Use the JSTO and local fire prevention plan to brief workers on work-center fire hazards, alarm reporting, extinguisher use, and evacuation accountability.

selectedModules.title: Jewelry / Loose Articles Restrictions
selectedModules.reference: Local procedures / equipment guidance
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Train workers on removing jewelry and securing loose articles when working around machinery, electrical hazards, rotating equipment, or snag hazards.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Use local work-center restrictions and equipment guidance to define prohibited items and exceptions for mission-essential tasks.

selectedModules.title: Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)
selectedModules.reference: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards, Chapter 14; 29 CFR Part 1910 - Occupational Safety and Health Standards (General Industry Standards) Subpart I; 29 CFR 1910.132; 29 CFR 1910.133; 29 CFR 1910.135; 29 CFR 1910.136; 29 CFR 1910.138
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Train each affected worker on when PPE is necessary, what PPE is necessary, how to properly don, doff, adjust, and wear PPE, the limitations of assigned PPE, and the proper care, maintenance, useful life, and disposal of PPE. Require workers to demonstrate understanding and proper use before performing work requiring PPE, and retrain when workplace conditions, job assignments, PPE types, or worker knowledge gaps make prior training obsolete.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Use the work-center JHA, BE occupational health assessment, manufacturer instructions, DAFMAN 91-203 Chapter 14, and local safety office guidance to identify PPE requirements. Supervisors must ensure PPE is provided, used, cleaned, inspected, maintained in sanitary and serviceable condition, and documented in JSTO training records. Cover eye and face protection, head protection, foot protection, hand protection, protective clothing, and respiratory or hearing protection when those programs apply.
